ENGLISH — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goes
   C. goed
   D. went

2. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

6. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

9. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

10. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

12. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

13. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

14. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. happiness

15. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1.2 Exclamatory and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Exclamatory and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.2.1 Reading for Information and Meaning and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
